headline: Day 38: Spark Pod Brings Cross-Lane Panic Bursts to Rootline Defense!
summary: May 13 introduces Spark Pod, a single-use seed-pod that arms in 1.5 seconds and unleashes a cross-lane burst upon enemy contact. This expands roster depth by providing a true panic button for multi-lane crisis waves, whereas Briar Pod remains restricted to its own lane. Board strategy now revolves around identifying synchronized swarm threats and managing tight economy to deploy Spark Pod precisely when two lanes converge. Encounter pressure is significantly heightened by wave 3's synchronized Spore Tick swarm, while the tutorial effectively onboard players to the arming window mechanics. Replayability deepens as players master placement timing, and visual asset quality is maintained with fully hand-authored art. The daily board feels hard-but-winnable without feeling doomed, as the tutorial directly prepares players for the challenge. We verified that the previous dated challenge roster cannot clear today's board without Spark Pod, confirming its load-bearing role in the canonical winning line.

candidates.title: Spark Pod - Cross-Lane Panic Burst Plant
candidates.summary: Add Spark Pod as a contact-triggered panic trap: it arms in 1.5 seconds, then the first ground enemy on its tile detonates a 3-lane by 3-column burst. It reuses Briar Pod's lifecycle while opting into cross-lane splash with splashSameLaneOnly: false.
keep: Reuses the shipped Briar Pod contact-trigger lifecycle instead of adding a second fuse lifecycle.
The splashSameLaneOnly:false config field creates a reusable path for future cross-lane contact traps.
mustChange: Keep Briar Pod's same-lane behavior locked by default so the old trap contract does not regress.
Publish manifest-backed Spark Pod art so the new gameplay-visible unit does not rely on fallback textures.
risks: Spark Pod could make scripted pressure too forgiving if the burst radius or damage is tuned too high.
The inventory chip should eventually surface the plant art directly, not only on canvas and Board Scout.

keep: A one-field opt-in on the existing contact path is the right size after May 12's over-scoped fuse proposal.
mustChange: Protect the same-lane Briar Pod contract with runtime UI coverage.
risks: Scenario tuning must prove Spark Pod is load-bearing rather than decorative.

keep: The player-facing verb is clear: place the Pod before a two-lane crisis and let contact trigger the burst.
mustChange: The tutorial must teach both the arm window and the restraint to save Spark Pod for crisis waves.
risks: A single-use plant needs crisp copy so players do not spend it on ordinary single-lane pressure.

keep: The runtime distinction between Spark Pod and Briar Pod is data-driven and easy to inspect.
mustChange: Board Scout and artifacts need to expose the cross-lane contract plainly.
risks: Validator proof remains important for any future retune of the dated board.

candidates.title: Tinder Fern Retry - Fuse-Timer 3x3 AOE
candidates.summary: Retry May 12's fuse-triggered Tinder Fern with a new trigger lifecycle, tile-box geometry, and a dedicated dated scenario.

candidates.title: Pollen Puff Retune for Two-Lane Swarms
candidates.summary: Keep the roster unchanged and tune Pollen Puff cadence and splash damage so the existing sustained splash plant handles the synchronized swarm wave.

winner.title: Spark Pod - Cross-Lane Panic Burst Plant
winner.summary: Add Spark Pod as a contact-triggered panic trap: it arms in 1.5 seconds, then the first ground enemy on its tile detonates a 3-lane by 3-column burst. It reuses Briar Pod's lifecycle while opting into cross-lane splash with splashSameLaneOnly: false.

rationale: Spark Pod won because it salvages the useful part of the May 12 panic-AOE thesis while avoiding the failed day's over-scoped fuse lifecycle. The shipped implementation adds a manifest-backed Spark Pod plant, a dated Spark Drill board, Board Scout visibility, and a data-driven splashSameLaneOnly contract: Briar Pod stays same-lane by default, while Spark Pod opts into cross-lane contact splash. That gives players a readable single-use crisis answer without inventing a new trigger or geometry system.

replyTemplates.whatIs: Spark Pod is a single-use Rootline Defense plant: it arms, waits for contact, then bursts across nearby lanes.
replyTemplates.howDoesItWork: It arms for 1.5s after placement. The first ground enemy to step on its tile detonates a burst that hits a 3-lane by 3-column area.
replyTemplates.genericQuestion: Briar Pod only hits its own lane. Spark Pod is the new option when two lanes are about to converge and lane-bound traps aren't enough.
